obscure

/uhb-SKYOOR/ - rhymes with secure · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Obscure means little known; attracting little notice.

The podcast celebrates obscure inventors whose patents shaped kitchens and crosswalks without ever carrying their names.

Example

The record book still lists an obscure 1930s pole-vaulter whose mark stood for forty years; his hometown paper misspelled his name both times it printed it.

Obscure here doesn't mean confusing — it means little known, off the map of common attention; an obscure fact, athlete, or byway may be perfectly simple once you finally come across it.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

unsung: Unsung means deserving fame that never came — the unsung engineer did the work while someone else took the bow. Obscure passes no verdict on merit: an obscure statute may fully deserve its obscurity. Unsung protests the neglect; obscure only measures it.

forgotten: Forgotten means once known, now dropped from memory — a name that was on everyone's lips and then slipped away. Obscure never had the audience to lose: an obscure inventor was little known from the start. Forgotten looks back at lost attention; obscure never drew it.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

famous: known to nearly everyone

renowned: admired far and wide for real achievement

Where it sits · how few people have heard of it

niche → obscure → unknown

niche vs. obscure: Niche is milder than obscure — a niche band has a small crowd that knows exactly where to find it.

unknown vs. obscure: Unknown goes further than obscure: the obscure poet has a few devoted readers, while the unknown one has none at all.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — ob-: over, against

Root — scur-: covered, dark (Latin -scurus)

Put it together: Ob- (over) + scur- (covered, dark) = covered over. What's obscure sits in the dark of public attention — until someone finally holds a light to it.

Use the root in a new word: chiaroscuro: The catalog essay devotes two full paragraphs to the portrait's chiaroscuro.

neutral

In this unit obscure means little known — obscure bands, statutes, dialects. Don't confuse it with hard to understand: a footnote can be obscure and perfectly clear. (As a verb it means to hide; you'll meet obscured and obscures in this unit's readings.)
